items.title: API (Application Programming Interface)
items.description: A set of rules that allows software applications to communicate and exchange information. APIs let products connect without building every capability from scratch.
items.example: A website uses a payment API to initiate an online transaction.

items.title: AI (Artificial Intelligence)
items.description: Technology that enables computers to perform tasks such as language understanding, prediction, classification, and content generation.
items.example: An AI assistant summarises a long document into key points.

items.title: Algorithm
items.description: A defined sequence of steps or rules used to solve a problem or process information.
items.example: A scheduling algorithm assigns tasks based on deadlines and availability.

items.title: Automation
items.description: The use of software or systems to perform repetitive tasks with reduced manual effort.
items.example: Automatically creating a CRM lead when a contact form is submitted.

items.title: Backend
items.description: The server-side part of an application that handles business logic, data processing, authentication, and communication with databases or other services.

items.title: Backup
items.description: A separate copy of data that can help restore information after accidental deletion, corruption, or system failure.

items.title: Business Intelligence (BI)
items.description: Methods and tools used to analyse business data and present useful information for decision-making.

items.title: Bug
items.description: An error or unexpected behaviour in software that causes it to operate incorrectly or differently from its intended design.

items.title: Cloud Computing
items.description: The delivery of computing resources such as servers, databases, storage, and software over a network, usually the internet.

items.title: CRM (Customer Relationship Management)
items.description: A system for organising customer information, interactions, sales activities, and follow-up processes.

items.title: Cybersecurity
items.description: The practices and technologies used to protect systems, networks, applications, and data against digital threats.

items.title: Conversion Rate
items.description: The percentage of visitors or users who complete a desired action, such as submitting a form or making a purchase.

items.title: Database
items.description: An organised collection of data that software can store, retrieve, update, and manage.

items.title: Dashboard
items.description: A visual interface that presents important metrics, trends, and operational information in one place.

items.title: Data Analytics
items.description: The process of examining data to identify patterns, answer questions, and support decisions.

items.title: Digital Transformation
items.description: The use of digital technology to improve business processes, customer experiences, and how an organisation operates.

items.title: Encryption
items.description: The process of transforming readable information into a protected form that requires the appropriate key to decrypt.

items.title: Endpoint
items.description: A device connected to a network or, in an API, a specific address through which a service exposes an operation.

items.title: ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)
items.description: Software that integrates business operations such as finance, inventory, procurement, and planning.

items.title: Experience Design
items.description: The practice of designing interactions and journeys so that products and services are useful, understandable, and satisfying.

items.title: Framework
items.description: A reusable structure and set of conventions that help developers build software more consistently.

items.title: Frontend
items.description: The part of a website or application that users see and interact with.

items.title: Function as a Service (FaaS)
items.description: A cloud computing model that runs individual functions in response to events without requiring the developer to manage a traditional server for each function.

items.title: Funnel
items.description: A model of the steps users take toward a goal, such as discovering a product, evaluating it, and completing a purchase.

items.title: Generative AI
items.description: AI that creates new content, such as text, images, audio, or code, based on patterns learned during training and the input it receives.

items.title: Git
items.description: A version-control system that tracks changes to files and supports collaborative software development.

items.title: GitHub
items.description: A platform for hosting Git repositories and collaborating on code, issues, and software projects.

items.title: Growth Marketing
items.description: An approach to improving acquisition, activation, retention, and other business outcomes through experiments and measurement.

items.title: Hosting
items.description: A service that makes a website, application, or other digital resource available to users over a network.

items.title: HTML
items.description: The markup language used to structure content on web pages.

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop
items.description: A design approach in which people review, approve, correct, or guide automated or AI-driven decisions.

items.title: HTTP
items.description: A protocol used for communication between web clients and servers. HTTPS adds transport encryption through TLS.

items.title: Integration
items.description: The connection of software systems so they can exchange data or coordinate tasks.

items.title: Internet of Things (IoT)
items.description: Physical devices with sensors or software that communicate and exchange data over networks.

items.title: Iteration
items.description: A cycle of building, testing, learning, and refining a product or process.

items.title: Information Architecture
items.description: The organisation and labelling of content so people can find information and navigate a product effectively.

items.title: JavaScript
items.description: A programming language widely used to create interactive web experiences and build server-side applications.

items.title: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation)
items.description: A text-based data format commonly used to exchange structured information between applications.

items.title: Journey Mapping
items.description: A visual representation of the steps, needs, and friction points a person experiences when interacting with a product or service.

subtitle: Key Performance Indicators to Knowledge Base

items.title: Key Performance Indicator (KPI)
items.description: A measurable indicator used to assess progress toward an important goal.

items.title: Keyword Research
items.description: The process of discovering the search terms people use and evaluating which terms are relevant to a website's audience.

items.title: Knowledge Base
items.description: An organised collection of information, instructions, and answers that helps people or software find relevant knowledge.

items.title: Knowledge Graph
items.description: A structured representation of entities and the relationships between them.

items.title: Latency
items.description: The time taken for a request, action, or data transfer to produce a response.

items.title: Large Language Model (LLM)
items.description: An AI model trained to process and generate language, often used for summarisation, question answering, and content creation.

items.title: Low-Code Development
items.description: Building applications using visual tools and prebuilt components, with some coding when needed.

items.title: Lifecycle Management
items.description: The process of managing a product, system, or data through stages such as creation, operation, maintenance, and retirement.

items.title: Machine Learning (ML)
items.description: A field of AI in which models learn patterns from data to make predictions, classifications, or other outputs.

items.title: Metadata
items.description: Information that describes other information, such as an article's author, publication date, or category.

items.title: Microservices
items.description: An architectural approach that organises an application as smaller services communicating through defined interfaces.

items.title: Minimum Viable Product (MVP)
items.description: An initial version of a product designed to test important assumptions with the smallest useful set of features.

items.title: Natural Language Processing (NLP)
items.description: Techniques that help computers analyse, understand, and generate human language.

items.title: Network
items.description: A collection of connected devices or systems that can exchange information.

items.title: No-Code Development
items.description: Creating applications or workflows primarily through visual interfaces rather than writing conventional code.

items.title: Normalization
items.description: In database design, a method of organising data to reduce unnecessary duplication and improve consistency.

items.title: Observability
items.description: The ability to understand a system's internal behaviour using signals such as logs, metrics, and traces.

items.title: OCR (Optical Character Recognition)
items.description: Technology that converts text in images or scanned documents into machine-readable text.

items.title: Open Source
items.description: Software distributed under a licence that grants specified rights to inspect, use, modify, or redistribute its source code.

items.title: Operational Efficiency
items.description: Achieving intended outputs while making effective use of time, resources, and processes.

items.title: Prompt Engineering
items.description: The practice of designing and refining instructions and context to improve the usefulness of an AI model's responses.

items.title: Productivity
items.description: The ability to produce useful results efficiently, with attention to quality and resources.

items.title: Progressive Web App (PWA)
items.description: A web application designed to provide app-like experiences through supported browser and operating-system capabilities.

items.title: Pipeline
items.description: A sequence of connected stages that processes work or data, such as a deployment pipeline or sales pipeline.

items.title: Quality Assurance (QA)
items.description: Processes and practices designed to help ensure that a product meets defined quality expectations.

items.title: Query
items.description: A request for information or an operation against a database, search system, or API.

items.title: Queue
items.description: A structure that holds tasks or messages until they can be processed.

items.title: Quantum Computing
items.description: A computing approach based on quantum-mechanical principles that may offer advantages for certain specialised problems.

items.title: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
items.description: An AI architecture that retrieves relevant information from a source and supplies it to a generative model to help produce context-aware responses.

items.title: Rate Limiting
items.description: A mechanism that restricts how frequently a user, application, or service can make requests.

items.title: Responsive Design
items.description: An approach to web design that adapts layouts and content to different screen sizes and device capabilities.

items.title: Return on Investment (ROI)
items.description: A measure comparing the benefit or return of an investment with its cost.

items.title: SaaS (Software as a Service)
items.description: Software delivered as a service, commonly accessed through a browser or app and maintained by a provider.

items.title: Scalability
items.description: A system's ability to handle growth in users, workload, or data while meeting its performance requirements.

items.title: SEO (Search Engine Optimisation)
items.description: Practices that help search engines discover, understand, and appropriately present web content.

items.title: System Architecture
items.description: The structure of a software system, including its components, responsibilities, interfaces, and interactions.

items.title: Technical Debt
items.description: Future maintenance or rework that may result from shortcuts, deferred improvements, or earlier design decisions.

items.title: Telemetry
items.description: Data collected about a system's operation, such as performance, errors, and usage events.

items.title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
items.description: An authentication method requiring two distinct types of evidence to verify identity.

items.title: Token
items.description: A value used to represent or verify authority, identity, or a temporary grant of access in a system.

items.title: UI (User Interface)
items.description: The visual and interactive elements through which a person uses a website, application, or device.

items.title: Uptime
items.description: The amount or proportion of time a service is available and operating according to its availability criteria.

items.title: Usability
items.description: How effectively, efficiently, and satisfactorily people can use a product to achieve their goals.

items.title: User Experience (UX)
items.description: The overall experience a person has when interacting with a product, service, or organisation.

items.title: Validation
items.description: The process of checking whether a product, input, or result meets its intended requirements or expectations.

items.title: Vector Database
items.description: A database designed to store and retrieve vector representations, often used for semantic search and retrieval in AI applications.

items.title: Version Control
items.description: A system for tracking changes to files and coordinating work across different versions.

items.title: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
items.description: A logically isolated cloud network environment in which resources and network access can be configured.

items.title: Webhook
items.description: An automated notification sent from one application to another when a specified event occurs.

items.title: Web Accessibility
items.description: Designing and developing websites so people with different abilities can perceive, understand, navigate, and use them.

items.title: Workflow
items.description: A sequence of tasks, decisions, or actions that moves work from a starting point toward a result.

items.title: Wireframe
items.description: A simplified visual representation of a page or interface used to plan structure and content before detailed design.

items.title: XML (Extensible Markup Language)
items.description: A structured text format used to represent and exchange data with custom-defined tags.

items.title: Experience Mapping
items.description: A method of documenting user needs, actions, pain points, and opportunities across an experience.

items.title: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
items.description: A web security vulnerability in which untrusted content is executed as script in another user's browser. Output encoding and appropriate sanitisation help reduce this risk.

items.title: YAML
items.description: A human-readable data serialisation format commonly used for configuration files and workflow definitions.

items.title: Year-over-Year (YoY)
items.description: A comparison of a metric with the corresponding period in the previous year.

items.title: Yield
items.description: The useful output produced by a process or investment, depending on the context in which the term is used.

items.title: Zero Trust
items.description: A security approach that does not automatically trust a user or device simply because it is inside a network. Access is evaluated according to identity, context, and policy.

items.title: Zero-Day Vulnerability
items.description: A software vulnerability for which effective remediation may not yet be available when it becomes known or exploited.

items.title: Zero-Code Automation
items.description: Automation configured primarily through visual tools or predefined actions rather than custom code. Exact capabilities depend on the platform.

items.title: Zettabyte
items.description: A unit of digital information equal to 10^21 bytes in the decimal system.
